title: Phones and gear
purpose: We know every phone, mount, and charger. We know where each one is and who has it. This includes the ones at a partner's location.
how: Every phone is enrolled in Apple Business Manager. We manage it through Hexnode in supervised mode. This gives us a live map of every phone. We can put a phone in lost mode and wipe it from far away. The collection app is locked in kiosk mode. App updates go out in stages, so an update from the client never surprises the whole fleet again. And the inventory record matches what we really have.

Partner fleets are enrolled too. The phones with the delivery partners belong to Vound. They are only kept at someone else's location. If a partnership goes bad, the MDM is the only control we still have over those phones.

There is one registry, and it is the only record we trust. For each phone, it holds the asset tag, the serial number, the IMEI, the model, the storage size, the condition, the current site, and the person who holds the phone now. It also holds every custody event: issued, returned, transferred, repaired, or lost.

breaks.do: First, find the phone on the MDM map. Put it in lost mode within one hour. You have 24 hours to get it back. After that, wipe the phone, file a police report, and update the registry. Any deduction follows the handbook, and only after Moharam has reviewed the case.

breaks.what: A site does not have enough hats or chargers
breaks.do: Use the spares in the kit first. Then get more from the store. A shortage is Mano's failure, not the site's failure. It is fixed the same day.

breaks.what: An update to the collection app breaks something
breaks.do: Every update goes to two test phones first. Always. The rest of the fleet gets the update only after a full test shift passes on those two phones.

breaks.what: Something is stolen at a site
breaks.do: The site agreement has a clause that makes the site responsible for theft at its location. Our property insurance covers the rest. Update the registry and tell the insurance company the same day.

breaks.what: A partner refuses to let us count the phones
breaks.do: We stop payment until the count is done. This rule is in the partner agreement for exactly this situation.

questions.q: Are partner phones really enrolled in the MDM?
questions.a: Yes. The phones belong to us. If a partner refuses, that tells us the partnership itself has a problem.

questions.q: Can a worker take a phone home?
questions.a: No. A phone is issued at clock-in and returned at clock-out. This happens every day. There are no exceptions.

questions.q: A worker lost a phone. Do we go to the police?
questions.a: Moharam decides, after he reviews the case. Any deduction follows the handbook. We go to the police only when a phone was stolen. We never use the police to pressure a worker.

questions.q: Why do we use supervised mode and kiosk mode?
questions.a: The phone has one job. Supervised mode lets us lock the phone to that one job. It also lets us find the phone and wipe it.

lifecycle.name: Enroll
lifecycle.text: Add the phone to Apple Business Manager and Hexnode. Set it to supervised mode. Lock the collection app in kiosk mode.

lifecycle.name: Tag
lifecycle.text: Stick the asset tag on the phone. Record the serial number and the IMEI. Take photos of the condition.

lifecycle.name: Registry
lifecycle.text: Each phone has one row. The row holds the tag, the serial number, the IMEI, the model, the storage size, the condition, the site, the person who holds the phone, and every custody event.

lifecycle.name: Kit
lifecycle.text: The phone joins a site kit after one 30-minute test session uploads.

lifecycle.name: Issue
lifecycle.text: The phone is issued at clock-in and recorded against the device number.

lifecycle.name: Return
lifecycle.text: The phone comes back at clock-out with a condition tick: the screen, the port, the mount, and the battery.

lifecycle.name: Repair
lifecycle.text: A spare phone takes its place right away. Broken phones go once a week to one repair shop. The shop returns them within 48 hours.

lifecycle.name: Retire
lifecycle.text: The phone is wiped and removed from the MDM. Its row in the registry is closed.

kit.note: Kits are put together at the central store. A kit is signed out as one whole set. Never start a site with a kit that was filled by taking items away from another site.

count.rule: Count on the same day every week, at every site and hub. If the numbers do not match, look into it the same day. If you still cannot explain the difference after 24 hours, put the missing phone in lost mode and report it to Moharam.
